- **Everyone in a lobby needs the same build, so update together.** A lobby admits only players
  whose build number matches. A b150 server still appears in a b155 player's browser, marked
  "the host must update", and the join is refused when you click it. Players who all stay on
  b150 can still play with each other.
- **Doors a client pressed and pressed without ever opening now open.** For anything the save
  file does not persist, the game invents a fresh internal name for every object each time it
  starts, so the host and the client were calling the same door two different things and the
  request died in silence — 110 objects per player, and in the case this was reported on a
  radiotelescope door took 72 presses and opened zero times. Doors, lights, light groups and
  storage containers are now addressed by a name both players work out identically, and all four
  agree exactly across peers. The same change repaired a single-player bug nobody was looking
  for: eight doors shared one invented name, so seven of them were unreachable to anybody.
- **Every lobby in the browser used to read "1/4" no matter who was in it.** The player counter
  was never connected to anything, for three months. It now reports the real count.
- **The joining screen shows the world downloading instead of saying "Connecting...".** Receiving
  the host's world is the longest part of joining — around 17 MB, so roughly 17 seconds on a
  typical link — and it used to render as a bar that said nothing was happening, next to a Cancel
  button. It now shows progress, so a join that is working no longer looks like one that is stuck.
- **A disc no longer comes back blank.** Picking a prop up, handing it over or ejecting it from a
  device destroys and recreates the object, and its own saved contents did not travel with it, so
  whichever player recreated it won with an empty copy. A prop's saved data now travels with it.
- **Discs put into a signal server survive.** Inserting a disc moves its whole state into the
  server box and destroys the disc itself; the destroy travelled between players and the state did
  not, so the other player's box answered an eject with "No floppy disc in the slot", and for
  anyone who joined afterwards the loss was permanent. Disc slots are now shared, empty ones
  included, so a joining player gets the true contents of every device.
- **A joining player can no longer overwrite the host's world with their own older save.** Their
  devices come up empty for a moment before the transferred save fills them, and that momentary
  emptiness could be published as the truth, erasing a disc the host had inserted since its last
  save.
- **The host's log no longer fills with false alarms while somebody joins.** It reported a failure
  once a second for the whole join for a message the network layer holds back on purpose, which
  made real warnings harder to find in a bug report.

Known limitations:

- A client's door opening is granted using the host's copy of that door, which has to be powered
  and unjammed. Power itself is not shared between players yet, so if a dish site's power state
  differs between you and the host an open can still be refused. The host's log names it directly
  if it happens.
- If the host refuses a coin-gun sale, the item is still consumed. The cause that made refusals
  common was fixed in b150 and they should be rare, but the sale is still not atomic.

This is a development prerelease. Please report what breaks:
https://github.com/VOTV-MP/Multivoid/issues
